maya: Quick signal — after we flipped the new kernel-selector heuristics yesterday, we've seen 95th latency up ~3-5% on large-context gen and a small number of GPU nodes hit OOM during steady traffic. :eyes:

maya: Short profile: kv-cache hit-rate for prompt prefixes dropped from 0.71 -> 0.58 on affected traces. That lines up with more frequent cache warm misses + bigger batches causing larger peak KV memory.

maya: nvprof snippet (aggregated):
```
kernel_selector: matmul_fast chosen 92% (was 48%)
avg_batch_size: 18 -> 26
kv_kv_bytes_alloc_peak: 14.8GB -> 18.6GB
mem_frag_est: +9%
```

owen: Hmm. matmul_fast was meant to be faster, but maybe it increases temporary workspace per invocation. Could be a per-batch workspace allocation pattern.

li: Do we have a diff of kernel workspace sizes? If matmul_fast uses tiling that allocates extra scratch, that would explain spikes.

sam: Also note batching heuristics bumped max_batch_window from 6ms -> 12ms in the same rollout. That could increase batch size and coalesce more prefixes into a single KV working set.

maya: Yep, both changes landed the same deploy. I measured per-request seq-distribution and it shifted slightly higher which pushes kernel choice threshold. So combo effect.

perf-bot: Regression alert: service=inference runtime=prod region=us-west-2 metric=tail_latency_95 delta=+4.1% window=2h

owen: Quick proposal: revert the kernel-selector change on canary and keep batching window change disabled until we measure workspace overhead. Re-enable one at a time.

li: Alternative: tune eviction/TTL to shrink in-memory KV for ephemeral prompts. We currently set prefix_ttl=600s and soft_evict=0.75. We could try prefix_ttl=120s + soft_evict=0.65 on canary to reduce GPU residency for low-value keys.

sam: Suggestion: add a small per-batch scratch-cap limiter in runtime: if estimated scratch > 2GB, force smaller batch split. Cheap guard vs OOM.

maya: I ran a quick sim locally with prefix_ttl 120s + forced batch_split at 20 and workspace guard at 2GB. Result: hit-rate recovered to 0.68 and peak mem fell to ~15GB; 95th lat improved back to baseline. No accuracy changes observed on eval set.

li: Can you paste the config snippet you tested?

maya:
```
runtime.tuning.kernel_selector: "canary-matrix-v2"
runtime.batching.max_window_ms: 6
runtime.batching.max_batch_size: 20
kv_cache.prefix_ttl_sec: 120
kv_cache.soft_evict_threshold: 0.65
runtime.scratch_guard.max_bytes: 2147483648
```

sam: Nice. If sim holds, we should ship guard + TTL change to canary cluster and rollback kernel-selector until we validate workspace.

deploy-bot: deploy started: canary rollout -> inference-canary-usw2 by maya at 2243001300

maya: Rolling now. I'll attach a small perf compare after 15m.

perf-bot: Canary monitoring: hit-rate delta (+) 0.07, peak_gpu_mem (-) 2.1GB, tail_latency95 (-) 2.9% (prelim)

owen: Good. Action items: 1) keep kernel-selector on hold, 2) bake TTL/soft_evict change for 48h, 3) implement scratch_guard BETA and triage any perf regressions from smaller batches.

li: I'll add a short perf test in the CI harness to measure per-kernel workspace allocations across batch sizes to avoid surprises.

maya: Thanks all — will post follow-up thread with longer logs if anything flares.

sam: tl;dr: combo of kernel change + batching window increased ephemeral working set -> lower prefix hit-rate + mem pressure. Mitigation = reduce TTL + scratch guard + revert selector until validated. :white_check_mark:
